correctness.rationale: With z=t−iw the nonvanishing STFT prefactor leaves the entire function with spectral factor exp(−πξ²) and the stated tone. The radial Gaussian logarithmic potential gives U'=4πF, where F=e^(−q)m+(1−e^(−q))θ. Differentiating using m'=4πv and q'=4πq(θ−m) gives the stated nonnegative intensity F', including its normalization for complex multiplicities. Exponential tilting concentrates at the essential endpoints: for each ε>0 the complement of the ε-edge neighborhood is exponentially suppressed by a positive-mass ε/2-neighborhood. The Laplace slopes give F(−∞)=min(a,θ) and F(+∞)=max(b,θ); when θ equals an endpoint both terms of the convex combination tend to that endpoint regardless of q. Finite mean gives integrable unit-cell counts. Phase-compensated time translation is mixing in the ergodic-theory sense by covariance decay between finite proper Gaussian vectors, and thus Birkhoff applies to the counts; monotonicity extends it to real T, and the exact means give L¹ convergence. Outside the band the strict sign and endpoint limits of log q give a unique balance, and at θ>b the balance satisfies log(1/|c|²)=4π(θ−b)w_c+o(w_c). Integrating the log-q derivative over bounded offsets gives q→exp(4πδs) locally uniformly, v→0, and hence the reflected-Gumbel intensity. Its integral is δ by substitution; reflection gives the other edge with the outward sign.

originality.rationale: The noncentral first-intensity formula is covered by the earlier general theorem on the overlapping PSD class and is not claimed as new. The supported distinct contribution is the compact-support noncentral endpoint and escape analysis, specifically the locally uniform weak-tone profile with its balance scale and excess mass. Neither the cited intensity theorem nor the centered ergodic law supplies that moving-frequency limit; obtaining it requires endpoint tilt concentration and a comparison at frequencies tending to infinity as the amplitude goes to zero. Birkhoff itself is standard.
